name: Wave direction (synthetic trade-wind fixture): median angle between the mean wave direction (UMWM mwd) and the WRF 10 m wind direction, wind > 3 m/s
source: waves in steady trade winds lie within tens of degrees of the wind; the bound is ours, about twice what the TEPEX-C cache gives (12 deg)

name: Wave direction (synthetic trade-wind fixture): median angle between UMWM wdir (the wind it was forced with), read as UMWM angles, and the WRF 10 m wind direction
source: UMWM is forced with this WRF wind, so the two directions are the same wind (math radians toward vs east/north components)

name: Wave direction (synthetic trade-wind fixture): median direction error of the Stokes drift from the restart spectrum (pipeline) vs summing cos/sin of UMWM's own angles
source: same spectrum, two ways to turn UMWM theta into east/north; Kenyon 1969, Breivik et al. 2016

name: Wave direction (synthetic trade-wind fixture): median speed of the Stokes drift from the restart spectrum (pipeline) / summed from UMWM's own k and dk
source: pipeline: deep-water E(f); reference: the file's own k(f)

name: Wave direction (synthetic trade-wind fixture): median direction error of the Stokes drift from the parametric spectrum (swh, dwp, dwd, mss) vs from the real restart spectrum
source: BRIEF 1.2/2.3: the parametric spectrum is the hourly stand-in for the 6-hourly real one; bound is ours, twice what the TEPEX-C cache gives (15 deg); a wrong convention gives more than 100 deg

name: Wave direction (synthetic trade-wind fixture): median speed of the Stokes drift from the parametric spectrum / from the real restart spectrum
source: surface.build multiplies the parametric field by the real/parametric ratio at every restart time
note: context: shown for orientation, never a pass
